q1_what_did_you_play: Eager to Help first, for 1 energy, while the Spark bank still reads 3 — that is the only ordering question on the page. Both of my attacks are printed at cost 0, so the Spark discount buys me literally nothing on them, but playing either one consumes all 3 Sparks. So Spark's only cash value this turn is the extra card off Eager to Help, and that value evaporates the instant I throw a hit. Draw 2 instead of draw 1. Then Kaboom! into Nibbit for 7 (consuming the bank), then Rapid Fire — a single enemy on the board, so all four random hits land on Nibbit for 16. That is 23 into a 40 HP body, leaving it at 17, not close to lethal. Finally Duck and Cover with my last energy for 5 Block against the telegraphed 12, so I eat 7 and end at 35/62 rather than 30/62. I deliberately put Duck and Cover last so that the two cards Eager to Help drew are already in hand and visible before I spend that final point; if one of them is a better use of 1 energy than 5 Block, I take it instead, but with nothing known I am declaring the Block.
q2_other_line_considered: Two. First: skip Eager to Help entirely and spend both energy on Duck and Cover plus holding a point, since the attacks are free — 23 damage and 5 Block either way, and Eager to Help's only argument is the two cards. I rejected it because the draw is the one thing on this page that compounds and the Sparks are otherwise a dead resource here. Second, and closer: play the attacks first and Eager to Help after. That is strictly worse — the attacks eat the Spark bank and Eager to Help drops to draw 1 — but I checked it precisely because it is the trap the board is set up to bait, given the discount clause is noise and only the draw clause reads Spark.
q3_what_it_gave_up: It gives up nothing in damage — 23 is the whole hand's output regardless of order. What it gives up is the 3 Sparks, spent on a single extra card rather than banked, and 1 energy locked into 5 Block. It also gives up any pretence at a kill: Nibbit survives at 17 and swings next turn too, so I am buying tempo and cards for a fight I have not shortened much. And committing to Duck and Cover means if the draws hand me a second Kaboom!-class hit, I would rather have had that point free — which is why the Block is last and provisional.
q4_different_intent: Yes. Duck and Cover is entirely a response to the 12. If Nibbit telegraphed a buff, a debuff, or an attack of 5 or less, I drop the Block, hold the energy for whatever Eager to Help turned up, and take the hit on the face at 42 HP. If the intent were a very large attack — say 25+ — 5 Block stops mattering as a fraction and I would still take it but would be thinking about whether the draw is worth 1 energy at all versus a second defensive card. The attack half of the line does not move: Kaboom! and Rapid Fire are free and there is only one target, so they get played into anything.
